sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold, unresolved. Fusion Klassroom is a rapidly scaling education-content and distribution business, but a paid-learner compounder is not yet demonstrated. FY26 revenue was ₹23.04 crore and reported PAT ₹7.60 crore; operating cash was positive, while cash after tangible and intangible investment was negative in each of FY24–26. The largest customer contributes 40.11%, so contract access and collections matter more than headline registrations. At the dated ₹161 close, conditional base/bull five-year returns are -13.84%/8.33%, before personal tax, versus a 15% hurdle. These are scenario outputs, not supported forecast returns: actual post-IPO cash/deployment and sustainable development economics are unresolved, so ordinary IRRs, R and all aggregate point scores remain NS. The next decisive evidence is a reconciled utilization/current-cash statement plus paid-cohort and development-spend economics. [S1][S3][Q1]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff 20 October 2026; dated quote 19 October 2026, ₹161.00, secondary historical close rather than a live executable price. Exact issuer: Fusion Klassroom Edutech Limited, BSE SME 544856, trading symbol KLASSROOM, ISIN INE1LMA01010. Incorporated 3 November 2016; converted to a public company 17 November 2025. The name and ISIN are matched to the eligible SM row of the official 19 October master, not an unrelated Fusion finance, software or engineering company. Current issued shares 9,316,873 imply ₹150.00 crore market capitalization. The ₹5 lakh reference is only a standardized liquidity test, not a recommended position. Lot 800 costs ₹128,800. Standalone Indian GAAP (AS) under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules is used, rather than Ind AS; no subsidiary/group business is added. Identity confidence is High; financial totals High/Medium, current funding and paid-cohort economics Low. G1 Conditional, G2 Conditional, G3 Hold, G4 Conditional. G3 Hold does not by itself bar quality comparison. Five investor years run 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, with a fiscal-year terminal stub explicitly modeled. [S1][S3][M1][M2][Q1]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 5, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 4, R NS, D 3, P 3 and L 2. GQS means Growth Quality Score. Exact Decimal arithmetic gives BQS known contribution 4.26 at 80% coverage, missing-data range 4.46–6.26; GQS 5.50 at 85%, range 5.65–7.00. IAS has 40% directly scoreable weight, known contribution 1.10, generic missing-factor range 1.70–7.10; carrying BQS’s own bounds through Q narrows the dependency-aware range to 2.565–6.165. All are NS, not midpoint scores or rankings. One-decimal half-up bounds are displayed separately; no intermediate rounding is used. No governance/funding-failure cap is imposed. A future resolved factor could change eligibility, not retroactively turn missing data into 5. The two judgment sensitivities move GOV by ±1 (BQS±.20) and EARN by ±1 (GQS±.15); missing-evidence uncertainty dominates those small changes. Full facts, contrary evidence and confidence are in the 13-factor audit. [E1–E20]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Klassroom combines recorded/live online teaching, offline academic coaching, exam preparation and skilling with institutional/channel distribution. An individual learner pays for access or tuition; a business/channel counterparty buys or distributes educational packages. Low ticket prices and multilingual content can widen access, but the economic unit is collected, retained revenue after faculty, distribution, support and content renewal, not an app registration. The prospectus describes online annual/enterprise pricing and ₹25,000–45,000 offline courses; these are product tariffs, not achieved net ARPU. FY26 reported online revenue ₹17.6196 crore and offline ₹5.4199 crore total ₹23.0395 crore. The category table separately identifies B2C ₹4.9213 crore; the rest is institutional/channel/other. Detailed labels on the next page do not reconcile to those online/offline splits, so the model uses only an explicitly conditional two-block revenue index, not invented learner counts.

The accounting policy recognizes B2B revenue when invoiced and rights are established, and B2C nonrefundable fees on receipt, on the stated basis that no performance obligation remains beyond granting access. Access lasting months is not automatically proof of an accounting breach, but the policy makes contract duration, delivery obligations, cancellation/refund practice and collection timing essential verification items. No unbilled revenue is disclosed. A contract-level invoice→access period→recognized revenue→collection bridge is still missing. [S1 pp 149,161–162][S3 pp 8–9]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The proposed advantage is reusable content combined with affordable access and local/institutional distribution. Mechanism: the same curriculum can serve more learners at low marginal delivery cost. Evidence: 30 centres,129 contents and a faculty/consultant network are disclosed, with fast recognized revenue growth. Durability is not established because curricula require refresh, platforms are replicable, teachers and partners can switch, and no paid-cohort retention or verified exclusive distribution rights demonstrate customer captivity. A capable competitor can license content, hire teachers and buy marketing; replicating local relationships takes time, but no quantified exclusion period or investment barrier is available. No dated addressable-market denominator supports a market-share or top-three claim.

Three primary competitors illustrate the alternatives. NIIT Limited’s FY26 release reports ₹390.2 crore revenue, ₹4 crore EBITDA loss and enterprise/consumer skilling, including AI offerings. Veranda spans commerce, schools and government test preparation with hybrid delivery; its restructuring makes a simple consolidated multiple misleading. PhysicsWallah’s 14 August 2026 filing reports FY26 consolidated revenue ₹3,899.54 crore and online/offline teaching segments. These establish competition, not comparable cohort margins or transferable valuations. Fusion’s 56.38% FY26 EBITDA margin cannot itself establish a superior moat when substantial content/data spending is capitalized. [S1][P1][P2][P3]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Recognized operating revenue was ₹0.6013 crore FY21, ₹1.6917 crore FY22, ₹4.8171 crore FY23, ₹4.5830 crore FY24, ₹10.0865 crore FY25 and ₹23.0395 crore FY26. FY24–26 annual additions were−₹0.2341 crore, +₹5.5035 crore, +₹12.9530 crore; growth−4.86%,120.09%,128.40%. The five-year FY21–26 CAGR is 107.34%, while the three-year FY23–26 CAGR is 68.49%. The five-year pandemic/early-development base is not used as the scoring anchor; the preselected three-year window has comparable restated revenue and includes the FY24 decline. A ten-year CAGR is ND. No reliably current FY27 interim or comparable TTM pair was recovered by cutoff. September 2025 revenue ₹12.3122 crore is H1FY26, not a current FY27 result; it must not be annualized and relabeled TTM.

REV starts 9 under the ≥30% schedule, has no trajectory adjustment, and is capped at 8 by Medium confidence. This is not an extra penalty for being small. Acquisition-driven changes were not identified in the standalone perimeter; a full volume/price/mix decomposition is still ND. Online and institutional access appear to explain scaling, but 659,048 registrations include free/demo/test/workshop users. “266,986 subscribers” times “₹991 average collection” implies ₹26.46 crore, more than stated online revenue, illustrating a mismatched horizon/denominator rather than proving falsification. Neither 58% reactivation nor 74,000 active users is verified paid retention. Category/subcategory and some older geography labels conflict; FY26 aggregate revenue remains reconciled. [S1][S2][S4]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The accessible opportunities are deeper institutional/channel distribution, conversion of existing users to genuinely paid access, expanded content and improved utilisation of centres/labs. Government-program beneficiary reach is not a contracted revenue backlog: ultimate payers, channel take rates, cancellation rights and acceptance/collection terms are not sufficiently disclosed. There is no verified opening backlog+orders−execution bridge to capitalize. The five-year model therefore grows monetized access indexes rather than fabricating student cohorts. Base annual revenue growth 20/18/16/14/12/10% separates an assumed 2% price/mix component from the residual access-volume index. Bear assumes an initial 30% sales loss, bull 30/25/22/20/18/15%; each has corresponding margins, tax, collections, inventory and reinvestment, not a TAM-only forecast.

The FY23–26 observed incremental operating-return proxy is about 41.48%: incremental NOPAT divided by ₹19.39 crore incremental invested capital, including content/data. Capex less D&A plus ONWC movement reconciles within ₹1,000 rounding. FY26 average-IC ROIC is about 51.4%, but neither measure attributes profits to individual new investments. Full development expensing adjusts both earnings and capital: the two-year FY24–26 proxy is about 41.1% from a loss base; the latest FY25–26 increment is about 11.0%, below the analytical 14–18% nominal capital-cost range. A full adjusted three-year measure cannot be established without reliable FY23 amortization detail. No paid cohort margin, CAC, payback or renewal series resolves that sensitivity. CAP remains NS, not a current-ROCE shortcut or a default 5. GQS remains NS despite strong sales growth. [S1][S2][S3]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Alka, Dhruv and Dhumil Javeri are the principal promoter executives; finance responsibility also sits with the managing director. The three named promoters’ post-offer share arithmetic is approximately 39.26%, not necessarily the complete promoter-group total. A current beneficial-ownership/encumbrance reconciliation, including subsequent SAST filings, was not successfully obtained; do not call the balance freely tradable or certify it unpledged. The prospectus reports no outstanding warrants/options/convertible obligations after the described conversions; advisory options were exercised and their shares are in issued capital. A bonus/split is not itself economic dilution. Current post-IPO shares, not old diluted weighted shares, determine the entry market value.

Governance concerns are specific. ROC narrative refers to delays 8–192 days, yet its table includes ADT-1 delays 2,958 and 2,324 days. GST filing delays are also disclosed. Management says these were regularized with additional fees and a full-time CS appointed November 2025; that remediation needs sustained evidence. FY24/FY25 director remuneration ₹.3060 crore each, relative salary ₹.0840 crore each and related-party rent ₹.1188 crore each total ₹.5088 crore,148.0%/17.5% of reported PAT respectively. FY26 director remuneration ₹.4950 crore, relative salary ₹.1136 crore and rent ₹.1069 crore total ₹.7155 crore,9.4% of reported PAT. A complete five-year remuneration series was not reconstructed. A ₹.05 crore promoter trademark transfer remained unpaid. These are related-party exposures, not proof of diversion. No material promoter loans/advances were disclosed. The auditor opinion is unmodified, and reappointment is not mischaracterized as a resignation.

Promises versus delivery: the earlier 25+centre footprint reached 30 inFY26; sales grew substantially. The July/August IPO proposed debt reduction and FY27/FY28 technology/content/labs/marketing spending. Those budgets are not commissioned capacity or demonstrated returns. Actual object-wise deployment and debt release are pending verification. The fresh issue, not the OFS, funds the company. No unsupported claim that all litigation/pledges are clear is made. [S1][S3][S5]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Restated FY24–26 revenue ₹4.5830/10.0865/23.0395 crore generated EBITDA ₹1.0153/4.0636/12.9900 crore, operating EBIT ₹.4857/3.2844/9.8976 crore and PAT ₹.3438/2.9042/7.6012 crore. EBITDA margins 22.15/40.29/56.38% rose far faster than ordinary delivery costs. Other income ₹.0409/.0193/.0626 crore is small and excluded from operating EBIT. Reported dilutedEPS ₹.50/4.14/10.41 uses historical weighted shares; it is not current post-IPO EPS. Gross profit is ND rather than an invented service/product-margin aggregate. Standard-tax operating normalization and a separate full-development-expensing sensitivity are both preserved alongside reported results.

CFO ₹.9384/3.5493/10.7140 crore was consistently positive, and the three-year ratio of sums to PAT is 1.4012×. FY26 CFO starts with ₹9.5120 crore PBT, adds ₹3.0924 crore D&A, ₹.4482 crore finance cost and ₹.2689 crore noncash advisory expense, removes ₹.0626 crore interest income, then absorbs ₹2.3860 crore working capital and ₹.1590 crore net cash tax. Inventory absorbed ₹2.7615 crore; receivables released ₹.0647 crore, payables added ₹.3807 crore and other current liabilities ₹.2288 crore. Current-tax accrual ₹1.5922 crore means low cash tax is not a perpetual cash margin. Net receivable-day proxies using average balances/total revenue are 0.07,12.00 and 9.96 days. Receivables are described as good and under one year; that is not a detailed 90/180 day ageing study. Inventory rose ₹.7148 to ₹3.4764 crore, substantially faster than sales. Product purchases/inventory are not a clean denominator for all education delivery, so an aggregate cash-conversion-cycle claim is withheld. Trade payable ageing shows FY26 amounts under one year past due; supplier-finance and maturity details need attention.

Cash capex ₹2.4992/4.0734/14.3716 crore produces FCF proxies−₹1.5608/−.5241/−3.6576 crore. Capex is investing cash flow, not an explanation for weak CFO. Financing interest is outside CFO and must still be paid. FY26 intangible expenditure alone ₹10.6658 crore capitalized content/data/software; ten-year content amortization assumes durable usefulness that needs renewal evidence. Expensing current intangible expenditure while reversing ₹1.8426 crore amortization reduces operating EBIT to ₹1.0744 crore and normalized PAT sensitivity to ₹.4686 crore. This deliberately harsh cash-reinvestment sensitivity is not a finding that audited recognition is wrong. Full-investment economics, not reported EBITDA alone, must fund growth.

Statutory/restated differences are reconciled: FY26 PAT ₹7.4993 crore plus prior gratuity ₹.1363 crore less tax ₹.0344 crore gives ₹7.6012 crore; equity ₹18.4492 crore less ₹.0345 crore tax gives ₹18.4147 crore. FY24/25 gratuity and share-issue adjustments are separately disclosed. Tiny ₹1,000–2,000 annual-report presentation differences are not escalated into material unreliability. Operating IC includes all recorded intangibles and ONWC, reconciled to equity+debt−cash/bank−income-tax assets+current/deferred tax liabilities. Opening net tax ₹.9008 crore is settled once in the model; existing operating dues stay inside ONWC and are not paid twice. Opening deferred tax ₹.6010 crore is retained as a nominal terminal claim once because a tax-base reversal schedule is unavailable; annual forecast tax does not separately reverse it. Restricted ₹.0050 crore bank guarantee cash is excluded. [S1 pp 211–224][S2 pp 225–226][S3 p 31]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹161 and 9,316,873 shares, equity value is ₹150.0017 crore. Current-share/FY26 reported P/E is 19.73×, not 15.47× obtained by using old weightedEPS10.41. The March-claims EV/EBITDA cross-check is 11.63× and P/B8.15×; these mix October market value with March debt/cash and are explicitly not certified current net-debt multiples. Reported total-capex FCF yield is−2.44%. Full-development-expensing PAT sensitivity implies about 320×, illustrating how the conclusion depends on recurring development economics rather than proving one correct normalized multiple.

The primary model starts from March 2026 cash/debt, adds net fresh IPO ₹27.5194 crore once, bridges disclosed July debt, repays ₹2.3561 crore inFY27 and remaining modeled debt inFY28, and pays interest at 17% with half-year repayment timing. OFS ₹7.40622 crore never enters company cash. IPO content/technology/lab budgets are minimums within capex, not additions on top of the same ordinary capital spending; marketing is already inside EBITDA and only a budget shortfall is incremental. GCP/acquisitions ₹5.9283 crore are spent once with no separately invented target earnings or asset recovery. Minimum cash ₹1 crore, no new ordinary financing, no dividends, and no assumed employee stock options are modeled. Tax 25.168% is applied to positive accounting earnings without unusable loss tax credits. Base EBITDA margin 44%, intangible cash investment 25% of sales and tangible capex 3.5% remain materially different from an asset-free software model. Bear uses 28%/35%/4% and 90 day collections; bull 52%/20%/3% and 15 days.

October 2031 cash and operating run rates interpolate March 2031/2032. The terminal operating DCF uses mature nominal growth 2/4/5% below business discount rates 18/16/14%, and continues development, tangible investment and growth WC rather than equating maintenance with depreciation. The 14–18% nominal rupee business-discount range is an analytical risk range for a concentrated, illiquid, early-scale business with high-cost debt, not a beta-derived WACC or the 15% equity hurdle. Base terminal FCFF ₹4.76 crore capitalizes toEV ₹39.64 crore; adding ₹33.18 crore retained cash less ₹1 crore minimum operating cash and ₹.6010 crore opening deferred-tax claim yields equity ₹71.22 crore, or ₹76.44/share. Conditional base/bull returns are-13.84%/8.33%. The full FY32 ledger extends beyond the investor terminal only to build the stub; funding feasibility is tested through October 2031 using earlier annual closes and interpolated terminal cash. A gap arising only after terminal does not disqualify that horizon. Bear fails minimum funding inFY2030 and has no ordinary return. Actual current funding remains unverified in every case, so all ordinary IRRs and R are null. Rescue is separately labeled, never used to imply ordinary survival.

A15% five-year hurdle requires ₹323.83terminal price and ₹301.71 crore equity. Holding base cost/reinvestment and valuation assumptions fixed requires roughly 74.01% constant annual sales growth in the reverse model, not a forecast. An explicit grid-and-bisection check confirms a funded crossing of the 15% hurdle; an unsuccessful search would return NS, not the search upper bound. Conditional base hurdle-entry arithmetic is ₹38.00, versus ₹43.37/₹33.41 at 12%/18%; none is an actionable fair-value target while funding/cohort economics are unresolved. The embedded 3×3 margin/development-spend and 3×3 discount/growth sensitivities rerun the full cash ledger. Entry and exit frictions of 1%/3% each reduce base conditional returns to-14.19%/-14.87%. [S1][S3][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest positive case is that a reusable content library, institutional distribution and IPO capital allow revenue to grow much faster than future cash development spend. The strongest bear case is loss/nonrenewal or discounting at the 40.11% top customer while content refresh, marketing and device purchases continue, collections slow and stored data/content realizes little liquidation value. In the linked bear, first-year revenue falls 30%, EBITDA margin 28%, intangible investment 35% of sales and receivables 90 days. Despite assumed receipt of net IPO cash, the ₹1 crore minimum is breached inFY2030; the annual ledger throughMarch 2032 shows a ₹6.13 crore peak gap. TheOctober 2031 balance is already negative. Negative cash is not an executable funding source, so ordinary terminal price/IRR is null.

The separate illustrative rescue issues equity at ₹80.50 with 3% issue costs whenever cash falls below ₹1 crore. It is not an available offer or promise. Additional shares dilute existing owners and the operating terminal FCFF is negative, so operatingEV is zero in that boundary; the minimum operating cash is not added as freely distributable value and the deferred-tax claim is retained. The illustrative rescue therefore leaves zero terminal common equity. A liquidation release of reserves is a different uncertain recovery calculation, not the going-concern case. A no-rescue insolvency/liquidation recovery cannot be established from book intangibles. Permanent-impairment risk is High, not a quantified bankruptcy probability. The decisive variable is sustainable collected contribution after content/data renewal and partner costs. A lower quotation alone does not prove those economics or locate missing cash. [S1][S3]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At unchanged current shares,5×/10× prices require ₹750.01/₹1500.02 crore terminal equity. Under base 16% business discount/4% mature growth and base terminal cash, that would require roughly ₹86.21/₹176.21 crore sustainable annual terminal FCFF, versus ₹4.76 crore in the conditional base and ₹14.18 crore in bull. That is not reached merely by repeating a student-registration count. A credible route needs much larger collected revenue, lower recurring development intensity, diversified renewals and funding without adverse per-share dilution. The enterprise-to-equity bridge is preferable to multiplying peak reportedEPS by a promotional multiple. Classification: speculative/unsupported at present, not mathematically impossible and not assigned a fabricated probability. [S1][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
At the next statutory results/utilization filing, reconcile bank cash, debt repayments, IPO proceeds used/unspent and investments by object to the original ₹27.5194 crore net schedule. Obtain a debt maturity/covenant/available-facility schedule; sanctioned limits less old drawings are not automatically undrawn committed liquidity. For sales, request top-customer renewal/collection status and paid subscriber cohorts: opening paying learners, additions, renewals, refunds, recognized revenue, cash receipts and deferred service obligations by access period. Reconcile pp 161–162 category labels before modeling channel ARPU. For development, separate maintenance/refresh from new content and purchased databases, document useful-life/impairment tests and demonstrate contribution after ongoing creation and customer acquisition costs. Track inventory ageing/markdowns and overdue supplier payments, not only receivable growth.

Upgrade triggers: verified deployment/current cash; diversified paid renewals; repeatable excess incremental returns after all investment; no renewed statutory delays; meaningful public-market post-IPO delivery. Downgrade triggers: customer loss, uncollected recognized revenue, capitalized spending outpacing usable content, tax/creditor arrears, unplanned related-party deployment, or dilutive funding. No numerical trigger is misrepresented as an automatic trade. Before any implementation, recheck BSE eligibility, surveillance, current lot, encumbrances, spread and bid depth, and recompute 20/60 session whole-lot capacity at the actual position. [S1][S3][S6][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold, unresolved; early-scale education/content exposure with material concentration and accounting/economic-normalization uncertainty, not a demonstrated compounder. BQS/GQS/IAS remain Pending evidence and must not be ranked as low numerical points. G1/G2 are Conditional, not failures; G3 Hold alone does not erase business quality. Here quality scores are independently incomplete because CAP and BAL lack adequate evidence. The price does not presently compensate for those gaps in the explicitly costed conditional base, and even bull fails the 15% hurdle. This is a research classification, not a personalized order or portfolio allocation.

Implementation is additionally constrained. A nominal ₹5 lakh is 3.88lots: floor 3 lots=2,400 shares/₹386,400; ceiling 4 lots=₹515,200. Fewer than 60 sessions exist after listing;49of 50expected sessions are observed, with 7August missing rather than zero. Since-listing low/high×volume bounds imply nominal continuous 5% exit 6.30–6.73 days, but this permits fractional lots. Recent 20 session median turnover is about ₹8.01 lakh as a close×volume proxy. At 5%, only two recent sessions accommodate one 800 share lot; average discrete capacity implies 30 sessions for the 3lot reference, while 2% permits no full lot in the 20observed sessions and 10% implies 6 sessions. Typical-day 5% capacity is zero. These historical constraints justifyL2; they neither guarantee future execution nor prove every session untradeable. No order is placed. [M1][M2][Q1]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The main financial evidence is the issuer’s final prospectus and separately published restated statements, checked against earlier restated/statutory history. Page/table locators and source hashes are retained. The official exchange master establishes identity, current shares, lot and eligible series, not all surveillance details. Daily price/volume is secondary because direct BSE19October bhavcopy requests returned AccessDenied HTML. Failed downloads are never treated as PDFs or corroboration. One missing listing-day observation is bounded, not silently dropped or changed to no trade; prelisting days are never padded with zeros. There are no verified live spreads, intraday executable bids, complete current promoter encumbrances or post-IPO bank confirmations.

The full inputs, annual historical and forecast ledgers, assumptions, sensitivities, exact score contributions, limitations and source registry are embedded in canonical JSON. Source and model QA check formula identities, funding flags, rounding, whole-lot capacities and reference integrity; structural validation is not external factual certification. All forecast price/mix indexes, margins, useful lives, tax timing, capex floors, minimum cash and terminal rates are explicit analyst assumptions. Neither a corporate promotional number nor the auditor’s clean opinion substitutes for economic verification. Raw source documents remain local; private backups intentionally omit PDFs, source HTML/OCR and shareholding files that may contain personal identifiers, preserving URLs/hashes and non-identifying analytical evidence instead.  [S1–S6][M1–M2][Q1]

existing_research.framework: Small-Micro-Cap Stock Research Master Prompt v3.0

factor_audit.name: Governance and stewardship
material_facts: Regularized but very long historic ROC delays and GST delays indicate control weaknesses.
Family remuneration/rent and promoter IP purchase require arm’s-length scrutiny.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Unmodified audit/restatement reconciliation, disclosed related parties and no reported promoter advances argue against treating these concerns as demonstrated fraud.
factor_audit.explanation: Mixed conduct and disclosure, not a governance-fail finding.

factor_audit.name: Competitive advantage
material_facts: Largest customer 40.11% creates partner bargaining power.
No verified paid-cohort retention, durable price premium or distribution exclusivity.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Thirty centres, reusable content and existing institutional access are useful capabilities.
factor_audit.explanation: Content/distribution is useful but readily contested; registrations and AI labels are not moat evidence.

factor_audit.name: Demonstrated revenue growth
material_facts: Comparable FY23–26 sales CAGR68.49%; FY24 contraction followed by two large annual additions.
FY26 growth 128.40% is recognized audited/restated sales, not beneficiary growth.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Five-year FY21 starting point is pandemic/development-stage distorted and channel definitions are inconsistent.
factor_audit.explanation: Rubric starts 9 at≥30%; no trajectory adjustment; Medium confidence ceiling 8. Three-year window preselected because FY21 pandemic operations are nonrepresentative, not because it gives a higher CAGR.

factor_audit.name: Accessible growth duration
material_facts: Academic/test-prep and skills demand create several plausible expansion avenues.
IPO budgets support content, technology and labs if deployed effectively.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Large customer/geographic concentration, unverified contract renewals and powerful competitors constrain access.
factor_audit.explanation: Some evidenced distribution and runway, but five-year access/retention is not proven.

factor_audit.name: Incremental capital efficiency
material_facts: Accounting incremental return depends on capitalization and attribution of rapid margin change.
Fully expensed sensitivity varies materially by window; no cohort contribution/CAC/payback evidence.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: High accounting returns and modest receivables are genuine favorable evidence, not dismissed as fictitious.
factor_audit.explanation: NS rather than default 5: economically meaningful incremental return cannot be bounded confidently from current ROCE or incomparable student counts.

factor_audit.name: Operating cash realization
material_facts: CFO/PAT ratio of sums 1.40× and short receivable proxy are positive.
Current tax accrual, noncash advisory expense and supplier credit support CFO; inventory increased materially.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: CFO is positive in all three recent years and receivables fell despite growth.
factor_audit.explanation: Mixed realization evidence; capital expenditure is investing, not an explanation of weak CFO. Low FCF is separately analyzed, not mechanically treated as poor collections.

factor_audit.name: Funding resilience
material_facts: IPO net cash is large relative to historical balance sheet but current available balance/use is not verified.
High-cost unsecured debt and expenditure schedules require a current debt/cash bridge.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Under stated assumptions base/bull can self-fund with IPO proceeds; that is favorable conditional math.
factor_audit.explanation: NS: hypothetical liquidity does not establish actual funding resilience or access to a committed facility.

factor_audit.name: Delivery and adaptation
material_facts: Recognized revenue and centre expansion demonstrate delivery.
Compliance remediation and prospective IPO projects remain different from a proven multicycle expansion record.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: No evidence of repeated failed formally dated guidance was located; absence of guidance is not itself a miss.
factor_audit.explanation: Mixed/early delivery; no execution bonus for unverified beneficiary counts.

factor_audit.name: Quality of profit growth
material_facts: Operating sales, not other income, explain most headline growth.
Development capitalization and long amortization lives substantially influence profit and per-share optics.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Reported PAT and dilutedEPS both increased, and other income is small.
factor_audit.explanation: Material normalization dependence: full current development expensing reduces FY26 PAT sensitivity to about.47 crore; this is not an audit correction.

factor_audit.name: Prospective return
material_facts: Conditional model embeds all reinvestment, tax, debt repayment and cash accumulation.
Actual post-IPO funding and sustainable cohort economics remain unverified.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Bull remains funded in the assumed ledger and creates value, though below 15% hurdle at entry.
factor_audit.explanation: No defensible point base return: ordinary IRRs and R remain NS, not mechanically scored from an optimistic hypothetical.

factor_audit.name: Downside resilience
material_facts: Loss of a concentrated customer plus slower collections produces FY30 funding failure.
Capitalized content/data may have limited transferable recovery value.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Net IPO proceeds could absorb substantial stress if available and discipline improves.
factor_audit.explanation: Material impairment risk at current price; rescue dilution is explicitly separate from an ordinary surviving-investor return.

factor_audit.name: Price-implied expectations
material_facts: Conditional base terminal value is well below the 15% hurdle requirement.
Reported P/E obscures a wide reinvestment/normalization sensitivity.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Revenue growth has been very strong and successful reuse could improve future cash economics.
factor_audit.explanation: Several favorable assumptions must hold together; no precise probability or unsupported target is inferred.

factor_audit.name: Liquidity and implementation
material_facts: 800 share lot is ₹128,800 at reference price.
Recent 20 days imply 30 sessions at 5% whole-lot capacity for 3 lots; typical day permits no full lot.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: 49observed days have trades; since-listing continuous-value estimate looks materially better.
factor_audit.explanation: Starting full-window 5–6 band downgraded for discrete lots and deteriorating recent capacity; not a claim every day is untradeable.

monitoring_plan.next_statutory_result: Next available FY27 results and utilization report; dates not assumed.
monitoring_plan.triggers:
At the next statutory results/utilization filing, reconcile bank cash, debt repayments, IPO proceeds used/unspent and investments by object to the original ₹27.5194 crore net schedule. Obtain a debt maturity/covenant/available-facility schedule; sanctioned limits less old drawings are not automatically undrawn committed liquidity. For sales, request top-customer renewal/collection status and paid subscriber cohorts: opening paying learners, additions, renewals, refunds, recognized revenue, cash receipts and deferred service obligations by access period. Reconcile pp 161–162 category labels before modeling channel ARPU. For development, separate maintenance/refresh from new content and purchased databases, document useful-life/impairment tests and demonstrate contribution after ongoing creation and customer acquisition costs. Track inventory ageing/markdowns and overdue supplier payments, not only receivable growth.

Upgrade triggers: verified deployment/current cash; diversified paid renewals; repeatable excess incremental returns after all investment; no renewed statutory delays; meaningful public-market post-IPO delivery. Downgrade triggers: customer loss, uncollected recognized revenue, capitalized spending outpacing usable content, tax/creditor arrears, unplanned related-party deployment, or dilutive funding. No numerical trigger is misrepresented as an automatic trade. Before any implementation, recheck BSE eligibility, surveillance, current lot, encumbrances, spread and bid depth, and recompute 20/60 session whole-lot capacity at the actual position.
